column1: # Labelled corpus for entity extraction from free text.
# Format: expected TAB text. `expected` is `-` for a text that references no entity, or a
# comma-separated list of `kind:canonical_id`. Blank lines and `#` lines are ignored.
# Labelling rule: the label is what a careful reader would conclude from this text alone. Labels
# were written before the extractor was run against them, and no label has been changed since. What
# changed in response to what the extractor got wrong is `spec/extractors.yaml` — which is the point
# of measuring, and is only honest as long as the corpus is the thing that does not move.
#   - A distinctive identifier is labelled even where nothing anchors it. `PROJ-42` is a tracker
#     key to anyone who reads it, so a text naming one references a ticket whether or not the
#     extractor can tell. Those lines are recall, and the extractor is expected to miss some.
#   - An opaque token nobody could classify is not labelled. `ab12cd34` alone could be an order
#     reference, a hash prefix or a coupon; a reader cannot say, so neither can this file.
#   - Near-misses are `-`: ordinary words that satisfy a loose pattern, digit runs that are
#     timestamps or quantities, standards names shaped like tracker keys.
# Grow it. A false positive found in the wild belongs here as a `-` line before it is fixed.
